approachQuestion.prompt:
First Character That Appears Once

The label `label` contains ASCII characters. Return the zero-based index of the first character that appears exactly once in the entire label. Return −1 if every character repeats or the label is empty.

Example 1: label = "cabacde" → 2 (the character "b").
Example 2: label = "aabb" → −1.
Example 3: label = "" → −1.
constraints: Each character is one ASCII character; compare characters exactly and treat uppercase and lowercase as different.
Do not modify the input string.
A character’s frequency is at most 200,000 and fits in a signed 32-bit integer.

options.text: Count each ASCII character in a 128-entry frequency array. Then scan the string from the beginning and return the first index whose count is 1.
options.feedback: The known, fixed alphabet allows direct frequency counts. A second scan of the original string preserves the requirement to return the earliest index.

options.text: Sort a copy of the characters and count each group. Then scan the original string and return the first character marked as belonging to a group of one.
options.feedback: This method can find the right earliest index because it checks the original order at the end. Sorting a copy is unnecessary: a fixed array for the allowed alphabet provides the same counts without sorting.

options.text: For each index, count how many times that character appears in the entire string. Return the first index whose count is 1.
options.feedback: The result is correct, but each new position causes the same string to be scanned again. One frequency count is enough to answer the question.

options.text: Check only characters that have both neighbors. Return the first one that differs from its previous and next character, or −1 if there is none.
options.feedback: Immediate neighbors do not reveal a character’s total frequency. For label = "abacbd", this method selects "b" at index 1 because it differs from both neighbors, even though "b" appears again at index 4. The first character that appears once is "c" at index 3.

feedback.reason: Choose a method that finds each character’s total frequency and returns the earliest qualifying index in the original order.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the method “Frequency Counts, Then Original Order,” choose one pair: time and auxiliary space. The alphabet has exactly 128 possible values; the input and returned index are excluded from auxiliary space.
constraints: Each character is one ASCII character; compare characters exactly and treat uppercase and lowercase as different.
Do not modify the input string.
A character’s frequency is at most 200,000 and fits in a signed 32-bit integer.

options.text: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space with an array of 128 counters.
O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Two scans still perform a fixed amount of work per character overall. The array has 128 counters, a size independent of the string length, so its space is constant under the stated alphabet model.
details: linear-constant: the tight pair for the fixed-size ASCII alphabet.
linear-n-space: this assumes a structure sized by the input length instead of the fixed alphabet.
nlogn-linear: this describes sorting a copy in option B, not the analyzed method.
quadratic-constant: this describes recounting the character at each position in option C.
Learning objective: Distinguish a character’s total frequency from its immediate neighbors, then return the earliest qualifying index.

methodReveal.title: Frequency Counts, Then Original Order
methodReveal.description: First count every character in a fixed array indexed by its ASCII code. Then scan the string from the beginning and stop at the first character whose count is one.
